KEY MESSAGE 1...Unsettled weather will continue through much of the 
week with occasional rounds of showers and thunderstorms, including 
some potential for severe thunderstorms Tuesday and Wednesday.

A persistent northwest to southeast oriented frontal zone over the 
Great Lakes will continue to bring an extended period of active 
weather through midweek. A multitude of low amplitude mid level 
shortwaves will traverse the northern periphery of a strong ridge 
over the central US, with each one bringing a period of enhanced 
ascent to the Great Lakes. The shortwaves will also modulate the 
frontal position, as will the influence of composite outflow and 
cold pools from passing rounds of showers and thunderstorms.

The elevated frontal zone will remain stalled just upstream through 
this morning, with associated isentropic ascent and moisture 
transport supporting occasional showers across Western NY and into 
the Genesee Valley and western Finger Lakes at times. Instability 
will remain very limited through midday, with just a small chance of 
some isolated thunder. Patchy fog will continue through mid morning 
in some areas before dissipating.

This afternoon through tonight, the frontal zone will move gradually 
northeast across the area, carrying the most widespread showers 
eastward with time. The most widespread rain this afternoon will be 
found from Western NY into the Finger Lakes, gradually drifting into 
Central NY and the North Country late today and tonight. Instability 
will remain limited today through tonight given extensive cloud 
cover and showers, but just enough tall/skinny CAPE may develop this 
afternoon through tonight to support a few isolated to widely 
scattered thunderstorms.

Tuesday through Tuesday night, northwest flow aloft will continue 
across the Great Lakes, with the frontal zone draped from the Nickel 
Belt of Ontario to central or eastern NY. Greater instability will 
develop Tuesday than recent days as surface temperatures climb into 
the 80s and rich boundary layer moisture arrives. Isolated to widely 
scattered showers and storms may develop Tuesday along lake breeze 
and other local boundaries with daytime heating and continue through 
at least Tuesday evening. That said, a lack of synoptic scale 
forcing and warm mid level temperatures may keep convective coverage 
limited. While SPC has maintained a slight risk of severe for 
Tuesday through Tuesday night from Western NY into the Finger Lakes, 
this risk may end up being quite isolated and conditional on 
sufficient forcing.

The most active day of the period still appears to be Wednesday. A 
stronger shortwave will move east across Ontario and Quebec, forcing 
a belt of stronger mid level flow to develop across the Great Lakes. 
Height falls and DPVA will spread southeast across the Great Lakes 
Wednesday afternoon through Wednesday night, with increasing large 
scale ascent. An EML plume is forecast to advect ENE through the 
Ohio Valley, with the northeastern tail of the EML possibly 
extending into the eastern Great Lakes Wednesday. 

Strong instability developing beneath EML induced capping will 
advect towards the eastern Great Lakes and help set the stage for 
potential severe weather Wednesday afternoon and evening once large 
scale forcing arrives and helps to overcome the EML induced cap. 
Forecast soundings show an impressive juxtaposition of moderate to 
strong shear and strong instability by Wednesday afternoon, which 
may support a notable severe weather risk. This potential is still a 
few days away however, and the finer mesoscale details and timing of 
prominent forcing will ultimately drive the evolution of convection 
and potential for severe storms. Stay tuned.

The mid level trough will deepen across Quebec Thursday through 
Friday, pushing the frontal zone south and west with time. There may 
still be a few scattered showers and thunderstorms Thursday as the 
front moves south across the area, followed by a return to mainly 
dry weather Friday as a more stable and drier airmass arrives from 
Canada.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Warm and very humid Tuesday through Wednesday.

Humidity will begin to creep upward today, with dewpoints rising 
into the upper 60s to near 70 across Western NY this afternoon. 
Extensive clouds and showers will keep temperatures in the 70s 
however.

Dewpoints will climb even higher Tuesday through Wednesday, reaching 
the low to mid 70s on the lake plains resulting in an oppressive 
feeling airmass. Temperatures will also climb into the 80s both 
days, with a heat index possibly reaching the lower 90s at times. 
The frontal zone will settle south again later in the week and help 
to remove the oppressive humidity, with dewpoints dropping back to 
more reasonable values Thursday and especially Friday.
